problem: Existing embodied navigation platforms target household/office scenes and define success as reaching an object center or nearby position, which ignores that lab instruments must be approached from their operating face with safe clearance from neighbouring equipment.
motivation: Biomedical lab robots must stand at a usable position in front of an instrument (centrifuge control side, refrigerator door) before manipulation can start. Standard goals and metrics encode neither operating direction nor clearance, leaving a gap between semantic object search and downstream lab interaction.
key_idea: Model every instrument with a three-zone envelope (body, safety clearance, operation area in front of the usable face) and use it consistently for scene generation, goal placement, success evaluation and trajectory safety metrics.
insight: Simple geometric frontier exploration already matches or beats the geodesic Oracle (74.4 vs 71.9 SR on MS-DEV) because of discretization error, and sampling multiple goal points in the operation area (3-Zone Oracle) raises SR to 83.3-92.5 and cuts unsafe proximity (VRT 4.9 vs 9.8 on DEV). VLFM fails mainly because rendered assets are texture-poor: GPT-4o names all instruments from text but recognises only 13.3% of rendered views, and recognition correlates with colour diversity (r=0.84). The centroid vs op-face ablation shows opposing per-split effects (+8.1 DEV, -18.0 VAL) that cancel in aggregate, so centroid goals can be unreachable behind walls.
method: Operational-face goal: g_i = c_i + f_i*(d_i+δ_i), placed at floor height, with δ 0.5-0.9 m; success if stop within an instrument-specific radius of 0.8-1.3 m
Three-zone envelope: Zone 1 AABB body, Zone 2 0.25 m clearance (non-overlap enforced in generation, violations scored in evaluation), Zone 3 operation area in front of the face

Dual-entry scene pipeline: P1 imports designer-authored GLB scenes annotated via the Blender LSAT addon; P2 procedurally generates scenes from an instrument catalog and layout templates via headless Blender, followed by semantic annotation, Recast navmesh and episode construction
Zero-origin GLB assets with wall-rotation formula θ=atan2(...) and placement rules; single-room and two-room templates give 47 scenes / 1,667 episodes with easy/medium/hard geodesic tiers
Safety metrics: MCR (minimum distance to any instrument over the trajectory) and VRT (fraction of steps within 0.5 m of an instrument)
Six baselines in a shared action space: Random, Oracle, Frontier, LLM-Frontier (DeepSeek), 3-Zone Oracle (8 candidate points in Zone 3), VLFM (Grounding DINO + GPT-4o + SAM)
Training interfaces: TrajectoryRecorder, PyTorch dataset, Gymnasium env with shaped reward including a clearance penalty; BC ResNet-18 baseline

setting.backbone: Mostly non-learned geometric methods (Frontier, Oracle); DeepSeek-chat (frozen) for LLM-Frontier; GPT-4o + Grounding DINO + SAM (frozen) for VLFM; ResNet-18 BC policy trained on Frontier trajectories
setting.training_data: none (training-free) for the main benchmark; BC baseline trained on 487 successful Frontier trajectories (7,142 steps) from MS DEV and Two-Room
setting.action_space: low-level: forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 30°, stop; 500-step limit
setting.simulator: habitat-sim 0.2.5 (Blender-built scenes; USD export for Isaac Sim)
setting.privileged: Oracle and 3-Zone Oracle use the navmesh and GT goal positions; the other methods use none besides the goal category

numbers.evidence: Table 5 (Navigation and safety results), MS DEV

numbers.extra: uses GT zone geometry and navmesh

numbers.backbone: ResNet-18 (ImageNet pretrained), single-frame RGB + goal vector
numbers.evidence: Appendix: BC achieves 41.9% SR (0.325 SPL) on unseen Multi-Scene VAL

numbers_note: The paper defines its own benchmark, so the split labels are approximations. The dev/val/test names refer to the paper's own MS DEV/VAL/TEST scene splits. VLFM's MS TEST entry is omitted in Table 5 because of API limits. Random, Oracle and LLM-Frontier rows exist in the table but are baselines or minor variants and are not listed.
results: Frontier reaches 74.4-87.5% SR, on par with or above the geodesic Oracle (71.9-79.2 on MS splits). The 3-Zone Oracle reaches 83.3-92.5% SR with lower VRT. VLFM reaches only 19.4-62.5% because of texture-poor rendered assets. The BC baseline gets 41.9% SR vs Frontier's 80.0% on VAL.
limitations: Flat-shaded, texture-sparse assets and low scene diversity (mostly 4 categories, no clutter); VLFM results are confounded by rendering quality
No sim-to-real transfer; only the BC baseline is trained and there is no RL result; small episode counts, so statistical power is limited (many McNemar p-values non-significant)
Strong baselines (3-Zone Oracle) use privileged navmesh/GT goal information; no instruction-language navigation, only category-goal
